long_biography.plain_text:
A neighbour's offer to buy the homemade candle intended for his mother gave Michael Kittredge his first proof of demand. Working from his parents' South Hadley home, he turned that Christmas-gift experiment into Yankee Candle. Holyoke Community College then encouraged him to treat the basement venture as a serious business.

Kittredge joined manufacturing to theatre, using fragrance, packaging and an elaborate South Deerfield flagship to make candle shopping an experience. After cancer prompted him to delegate daily control, he sold the company in 1998 and later stepped away from its board. He eventually returned to the craft by helping his son establish Kringle Candle. Kittredge also directed substantial support toward education and health institutions in western Massachusetts, where college and hospital buildings carry his name.
